homePage.missionQuote: “Cheap and good might exist — but without knowledge and transparency, it could become the most expensive trap you ever fall into.”
homePage.missionExplanation:
In a world where true cost matters and quality is tangible, we believe that honest pricing is far more valuable than just an attractive number. Especially when details like thread count per square inch directly affect softness, durability, and long-term use.

qualityVsPrice.title: Superior Quality with Technical Data for Confident Decision-Making
qualityVsPrice.p1: Our products are meticulously designed and developed at every stage, from material selection and production processes to quality inspection standards, to meet the needs of those who value a rewarding and sustainable long-term user experience.
qualityVsPrice.p2: One of the key elements we present with transparency is the Thread Count (TC) standard, which we calculate according to international methods and state clearly on the product label to ensure mutual understanding and prevent consumer confusion.
qualityVsPrice.p3: While many retailers may display very high TC values, such as 600 TC, to create an image of luxury, this can result from counting multi-ply threads or measuring in a smaller-than-standard area, like 1 square inch, without proper conversion. This inflates the numbers without reflecting the true quality of the fabric, potentially distorting product comparisons.
qualityVsPrice.p4: For materials, we select high-quality natural fibers such as 100% Combed Cotton, TENCEL™, and Bamboo Rayon that are OEKO-TEX® certified, free from irritating residues, even for sensitive skin. This is combined with High-Density Weave technology, which makes the fabric soft, dense, not thin, wrinkle-resistant, and breathable.
qualityVsPrice.p5: In terms of craftsmanship, we use a Double-Stitch technique to enhance strength and durability for long-term use, along with designing sizes to fit various mattress types, accommodating both depth and height, ensuring they don't slip off and remain smooth after use.
qualityVsPrice.p6: Although our products may have a price point that reflects their fine craftsmanship and high production quality, what customers receive in return is long-term value, confidence in safety, and beauty that does not diminish even after years of use.

tencel.advantage3: Naturally reduces the growth of bacteria for better hygiene.

item1.title: 'Higher Thread Density = Always Better?'
item1.content: Not always true! Fabric quality is not measured by density alone but also depends on other crucial factors:
item1.point1: Fiber Type: For example, long-staple cotton is better than short-staple.
item1.point2:
Weave and Finishing: Such as Sateen or Percale and the process of softening the fabric.

Example: A 700 threads/10cm² Cotton fabric using genuine long-staple fibers may feel softer and more durable than a 1300 threads/10cm² fabric using low-quality fibers.

item2.title: 'Is Tencel = Artificial Silk?'
item2.content: Incorrect. Tencel™ (Lyocell) is a fiber made from natural wood pulp (Cellulose) through an environmentally friendly process, not a synthetic fiber like Polyester. Although it has a silk-like softness and smoothness, its standout features are breathability and moisture management, which help reduce bacteria growth better than real silk.

item3.title: 'Are White Sheets Prone to Stains and Hard to Care For?'
item3.content: On the contrary, white has several advantages:
item3.point1: Standard of Cleanliness: It's the easiest color to spot stains on, making it the standard for 5-star hotels worldwide to guarantee true hygiene and cleanliness.
item3.point2: Care and Maintenance: Good quality white fabric can withstand gentle bleaching to maintain its brightness better than dark-colored fabrics that might fade from chemicals.

shopTips.title: ✨ Our Shop's Tips for Choosing Bedding ✨

tip1.segment1: Don't judge a fabric by its picture or density number alone! If unsure,
tip1.segment2: to ask about the fabric and thickness before deciding, especially for large orders.

shopTips.tip2: Avoid fabrics made from short-staple Cotton or low-quality Polyester Blends, as they tend to pill easily and shed during washing, leading to a short lifespan and discomfort.
shopTips.tip3: A Sateen weave will give a soft, slightly glossy surface, ideal for luxury. A Percale weave will provide a firm, crisp, and cool feel, suitable for hot weather and those who prefer freshness.
shopTips.tip4: Beware of overly inflated density numbers, as it's often achieved by counting multi-ply threads as single threads, making the fabric too thick and heavy, stuffy, and not adding to comfort. Focus on fiber quality and weave.
shopTips.tip5: Consider the thickness of your mattress: Choose a fitted sheet with a pocket depth appropriate for your mattress thickness to ensure a snug fit that doesn't slip off easily.

item1.q: How do hotel bed sheets differ from regular ones?
item1.a: Hotel sheets often use higher quality fibers (e.g., Long-Staple Cotton, Tencel™), a thread density suitable for durability and frequent washing, are resistant to heat and chemicals, have stronger stitching, and favor white or solid colors for a clean, luxurious look.

item2.q: Which type of Cotton is best for hotels?
item2.a: “Combed Cotton” from long fibers (like Egyptian or Pima Cotton) is a high standard for hotel sheets because it's soft, durable, breathable, and doesn't pill easily after many washes.

item3.a: Tencel™ fabric is significantly more wrinkle-resistant than Cotton and provides a soft, glossy feel without heavy ironing. Cotton-Polyester blends (like our CVC or Soft-Tex™) are also wrinkle-resistant and easy to care for, ideal for those who dislike ironing or hotels looking to reduce care steps.

item4.q: How to care for different types of bed sheets?
item4.a: Generally, wash in cool or warm water (up to 40°C), use a low spin cycle, air dry in the shade or tumble dry on low heat, and avoid chlorine bleach on colored fabrics. However, please refer to the specific care instructions on the product label or ask us.

whatIsTencelPage.mainTitle: What is Tencel™ Lyocell? The Secret to Superior Sleep
whatIsTencelPage.mainDescription: Discover the wonders of Tencel™, a natural cellulose fiber that offers unparalleled softness, hygiene, and environmental friendliness. Immerse yourself in blissful sleep every night.

introSection.title: What is Tencel™ and Why is it Special?

whatIsIt.intro: Tencel™ is the brand name for Lyocell and Modal fibers, produced by the Austrian company Lenzing AG. These fibers have a fascinating origin and production process:
whatIsIt.point1: From Nature to Fiber: Produced from the cellulose of wood pulp, primarily from sustainably managed eucalyptus or beech trees.
whatIsIt.point2: Eco-Friendly Production: The Tencel™ Lyocell production process won the European Award for the Environment for its closed-loop system, which recycles over 99% of its non-toxic solvent and uses significantly less water than conventional cotton production.
whatIsIt.point3: Unique Nanofibril Structure: The result is a high-purity fiber with this special structure, which gives Tencel™ fabric many remarkable properties not found in other fabrics.

whatIsTencelPage.featuresTitle: Key Features of Tencel™ Fabric You'll Love

item1.title: Silky Smooth, Luxurious Feel
item1.description: Tencel™ has an exceptionally smooth and soft surface, providing superior skin comfort, like a gentle caress, creating a luxurious sleep experience.

item2.title: Excellent Breathability for a Cool Night
item2.description: Tencel™'s nanofibril structure efficiently absorbs and releases moisture, keeping you cool and dry all night, perfect for hot and humid climates.

item3.title: Reduces Bacterial Growth for Better Hygiene
item3.description: The superior moisture management creates an environment that is naturally unfavorable for the growth of bacteria and dust mites, reducing odors and giving you confidence in its cleanliness.

item4.title: Gentle on Sensitive Skin, Like a Soothing Embrace
item4.description: Its smooth surface and fiber purity make Tencel™ ideal for sensitive skin, including children and the elderly, minimizing irritation.

item5.title: Vibrant Colors, Long-Lasting
item5.description: Tencel™ fibers absorb dye exceptionally well, resulting in vibrant, long-lasting colors, even after many washes, keeping your bedding looking new.

care.title: Caring for Your Tencel™ Fabric for Lasting Beauty
care.intro: To maintain the beauty and excellent properties of your Tencel™ fabric for a long time:
care.item1: Washing: Wash in cool or warm water (up to 30-40°C) on a gentle cycle. Use a laundry bag to reduce friction.
care.item2: Detergent: Use a mild detergent. Avoid chlorine bleach.
care.item3: Drying: Tumble dry on low heat or line dry in a shaded, breezy area. Avoid prolonged direct sunlight.
care.item4: Ironing: If necessary, iron on low to medium heat, preferably while slightly damp or using a pressing cloth.

firstWash.title: First Wash and Use Instructions for Hotel Towels
firstWash.intro: To ensure hotel towels perform at their best from the first use and to extend their lifespan, follow these guidelines:
firstWash.step1_reason: Technical Reason: New towels from the factory are often coated with chemicals (like softener or wax) to prevent dust during storage, which reduces absorbency.
firstWash.step1_practice_item1: Wash towels in 40–60°C water before use.
firstWash.step1_practice_item2: Avoid using fabric softener in the first wash as it will coat the fibers and reduce absorbency.
firstWash.step1_practice_item3: It is recommended to add ½ cup of distilled vinegar instead of softener in the first cycle to help open up the fibers and reduce any chemical residue.
firstWash.step2_item1: Wash towels separately from other items like clothes, bed sheets, or items with zippers/buttons to avoid friction that could cause linting.
firstWash.step2_item2: Avoid washing with dark-colored fabrics to prevent color bleeding onto white towels.
firstWash.step3_item1: Use a mild, non-bio or low-sudsing detergent that won't damage the cotton fibers.
firstWash.step3_item2: If extra whitening is needed, opt for an oxygen-based bleach instead of chlorine bleach.
firstWash.step4_item1: Use a medium heat setting for drying to prevent shrinkage or stiffness.
firstWash.step4_item2: If using a dryer, add dryer balls to help fluff the towel fibers and prevent them from clumping.
firstWash.step5_item1: Wash towels every 1–2 days of use to prevent bacteria and odor buildup.
firstWash.step5_item2: Avoid drying in damp, shaded areas or in direct, strong sunlight for too long, as this can make the fabric brittle or fade.
firstWash.step6_item1: Don't cram the washing machine with too many towels. Overloading prevents proper rinsing, leaving detergent residue that makes towels stiff and less absorbent. Wash in smaller loads for better results.
firstWash.step7_item1: Before washing a full load, inspect towels for any stains (e.g., makeup, oil). Pre-treat these stains with a suitable stain remover. Washing can set stains permanently, especially if dried with heat.
firstWash.step8_item1: Fold towels promptly after they are completely dry to prevent wrinkles. Store them in a well-ventilated, dry linen closet. Avoid storing them in plastic bags, which can trap moisture and lead to mildew.
firstWash.step9_item1: For hotels and high-use environments, regularly rotate your stock of towels. This ensures even wear and tear across all towels, extending the overall life of your inventory instead of overusing a few favorites.
firstWash.step10_item1: If towels become stiff or musty over time, run them through a wash cycle with hot water and one cup of white vinegar (no detergent). Follow with a second cycle using hot water and half a cup of baking soda (no detergent). This strips residue and restores softness.
firstWash.conclusion: ✅ Summary: Washing towels correctly the first time helps them achieve maximum absorbency, prevents residual odors, and reduces long-term linting or pilling. Ideal for hotels looking to maintain quality and a professional, clean brand image.

tip1.title: Machine wash warm (max 60°C) with similar colors
tip1.explanation: Warm water effectively cleans towels without damaging the fibers. We advise separating colors to prevent any fading and suggest adding a bit of baking soda to the wash to enhance brightness and remove odors.

tip2.title: Avoid bleach or optical brighteners
tip2.explanation: Harsh chemicals like bleach and optical brighteners can damage the cotton fibers, reducing the towel's lifespan and softness. For long-term durability and guest safety, we recommend using a mild, bleach-free detergent.

tip3.title: Tumble dry low or hang to air-dry
tip3.explanation: Use a low heat setting when tumble drying to prevent fiber breakdown and stiffness. For maximum energy efficiency and to maintain the fabric's natural softness, hanging them to air-dry is an excellent alternative.

tip4.title: Do not use fabric softeners – it may reduce absorbency
tip4.explanation: Fabric softeners work by coating the fibers, which unfortunately blocks their ability to absorb moisture. To maintain natural fluffiness, try adding a cup of white vinegar to the rinse cycle instead.

tip5.title: Replace towels every 12–18 months for best hygiene
tip5.explanation: Over time and after many washes, towels naturally lose their effectiveness. We recommend regular replacement to ensure your guests always experience maximum softness, hygiene, and satisfaction. Old towels can be repurposed for cleaning to promote sustainability.
